messages.author: 81e3fe85cdfef3f4
messages.subject: latent field and observations differ
parts:
Dear all, 
I created a simple binomial model with only a intercept and a latent field: 

f2 <- y ~ -1 + Intercept + f(w, model = spde)
M1_nb <- inla(f2,
           family = "nbinomial",
           data = inla.stack.data(Stk),
           control.compute = list(dic = TRUE,
                                  waic = TRUE,
                                  config = TRUE),
           control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(Stk)), verbose = F)

However when plotting the latent field the patterns seems to differ from the observations (size of cirkels is corresponding to the counts, black dots are locations where counts = 0):

See for example, the red area around 6000 km y-axis or the blue area at 5850. I don't really get how this is possible. I tried to change number of vertices and the distance to the border of mesh, but without any significant effect. Anyone has an idea how this is possible? You would almost say that the input observations are different from the plotted observations in this plot (but that's not the case).

Regards, Bram Parmentier

code for plotting latent field:
w.pm1 <- M1_nb$summary.random$w$mean
wproj <- inla.mesh.projector(mesh,  dims = c(1000, 1000))
w.pm1000_1000 <- inla.mesh.project(wproj, w.pm1)
Grid <- expand.grid(Xkm = wproj$x,
                    Ykm = wproj$y)
Grid$w.pm <- as.vector(w.pm1000_1000)

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] latent field and observations differ
parts:
Hi,
Hard to tell where the problem is. You can check the result with family=“normal”.
Even though that’s a different model, the qualitative behaviour should be similar, so that you can see if there is still an apparent spatial mismatch or not. If there is, then it’s likely that it’s the model setup that has a problem, rather than the estimation.

Finn
